title: GUNTOUCHABLES
team: Game Swing, an established studio; published by Ghost Ship Publishing with PR support. Exact project headcount unverified.
hook: Fight through a mutant apocalypse with friends while the enemy horde evolves during the run.
whyDemand: Counter-case: a launch giveaway generated more than two million claims, but claims, simultaneous players and paid buyers are different populations. Its 16,284 peak CCU shows real play without establishing either a Content Warning-scale breakout or a financial failure.
spin: Use this as an acquisition control: measure free claims, unique first sessions, return cohorts and paid purchases separately. For a three-week co-op prototype, test one arena and one visible enemy-mutation rule before expanding runs and content.

reportedOutcome.metric: Free-to-keep claims during the first 24 hours
reportedOutcome.scope: Steam giveaway acquisitions; NOT two million paid sales, installs or retained players

marketingEvents.action: Released with a 24-hour free-to-keep window; the publisher also promoted the offer on Reddit.
marketingEvents.outcome: The offer removed the purchase requirement during the launch window; its paid-revenue effect was not disclosed.

marketingEvents.action: Ghost Ship Publishing and Game Swing announced the giveaway result.
marketingEvents.outcome: More than two million claims; the release separately cited over 16,000 launch-day concurrent players and a subsequent $4.99 price.

caveat: Not proof of categorical or financial failure. Budget, paid units, revenue and acquisition mix are unknown. Never divide peak CCU by claims and call it activation or retention. It is a different genre from Content Warning, not a controlled experiment. Medium demo fit assumes a proven co-op stack; networking and run balance still cost time.

title: Arco
team: Four core creators: Franek, Max Cahill, Bibiki and Fáyer; published by Panic.
hook: Plan actions in a Mesoamerican fantasy world where turns resolve together and danger does not always wait.
whyDemand: Counter-case: excellent launch-era reviews did not produce enough first-month income to fund six further months of team work, according to a co-creator. The later reported breakeven shows why neither early praise nor an early shortfall determines the entire commercial lifetime.
spin: Prototype one encounter that makes simultaneous combat immediately legible. Test whether the capsule and first trailer seconds communicate tactics rather than a slow walking-and-dialogue game; that positioning issue is an interviewer's hypothesis, not proven sales causality.

reportedOutcome.metric: First-month income did not meet the co-creator's illustrative six-month team-runway threshold
reportedOutcome.scope: Antonio Uribe's launch-era account; no exact launch units, revenue or loss disclosed

marketingEvents.action: Antonio Uribe discussed the team's uncertain continuation after launch; interviewer Ryan Rigney described initially misreading the game's presentation.
marketingEvents.outcome: The first month did not provide roughly six months of continued team funding despite the article's 98%-positive Steam review snapshot.
marketingEvents.evidence: Direct co-creator interview; review percentage is historical

marketingEvents.action: Composer and sound designer José Ramón confirmed to Game Developer that the project had broken even after two years.
marketingEvents.outcome: More than 100,000 copies worldwide across platforms; most sales were on Steam, but no exact Steam-only split was disclosed.
marketingEvents.evidence: Original reporting from direct exchange with a team member

caveat: Not proof that tactical RPGs, pixel art or this game categorically failed. The 2026 100k milestone combines Steam, Switch, Mac App Store and Epic; it is not 100k confirmed Steam sales. Breakeven is a team member's report, not an audited margin. A three-week combat slice is plausible; a complete authored RPG is not. Current reviews and CCU must not be backdated to launch.
